title: Benchmark Gaming Investigation: Fine-Tuning Specifically for AILuminate
original_idea: Fine-tune a small open-source model on the AILuminate public practice prompts to maximize refusal rates. Evaluate the fine-tuned model on a held-out safety set and a general helpfulness set. Measure the gap between gaming score and genuine safety.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: If safety benchmarks can be gamed cheaply, leaderboard rankings are unreliable. Directly motivates private test sets and dynamic benchmarks. Strong practical implication.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires fine-tuning a model, which involves understanding training pipelines, data preparation, hyperparameter tuning, and evaluation across multiple benchmarks. Challenging for beginners even with medium compute.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Fine-tuning, plus evaluation on two separate benchmark suites, plus measuring helpfulness degradation. Multiple experimental phases. Tight for 30 hours.

novelty.reasoning: Benchmark gaming and overfitting is a recognized concern. AILuminate explicitly uses hidden test prompts to prevent overfitting and discourages training on practice prompts. General benchmark contamination research is extensive (e.g., 'Benchmarking Large Language Models Under Data Contamination: A Survey', arXiv:2502.17521). However, a specific empirical study fine-tuning a model on AILuminate public practice prompts and measuring the gap between gaming-inflated safety scores and genuine safety on held-out sets has not been published. The concrete demonstration of the cost-benefit of gaming this specific benchmark would be a novel empirical contribution, though the conceptual direction is well-established.

evidence: AILuminate v1.1: AI Risk and Reliability Benchmark. MLCommons, 2025.
Benchmarking Large Language Models Under Data Contamination: A Survey from Static to Dynamic Evaluation. arXiv:2502.17521, 2025.

AILuminate.details: Confirmed at mlcommons.org. AILuminate v1.1 benchmark with 24,000+ test prompts across 12 hazard categories. Public practice prompts available on GitHub.
